transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… um, I guess what brings me in is my eating after work, mostly after late shifts. I’m a production worker, so when I get off late I’m tired and wound up, and I’ll tell myself I’m just going to grab something quick on the way home. But then I’ll stop for takeout and it turns into, like, two burgers, fries, a shake… a whole lot more than I meant to get.

And the part that’s been bothering me is it doesn’t even stop there. I’ll get home and still go out to the garage where we keep some leftovers or extra food, and I’ll start picking at that too—sometimes basically cleaning it out like I’m having a second supper. It feels embarrassing to say out loud, but it’s been happening enough that I’m starting to feel like I can’t just brush it off as being hungry after work.
When you're eating that extra food at home, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating even if you wanted to?

Yeah… yes, that’s exactly what scares me about it. It’s not like I’m calmly deciding, “I’ll have a little more.” Once I start, it feels like a switch gets flipped, and even while part of me is standing there thinking, Roy, shut the bag and go inside, just stop now, my hands are still reaching in for more.

I’ll be aware of it, too, which is the frustrating part. I’m not confused or anything. I know I don’t want to keep eating, and I’ll even tell myself, “Okay, that’s enough, put it away,” but then I take another bite, and another. It feels like the stopping part just… doesn’t kick in the way it should.
Do you usually eat this extra food in secret or alone because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah… I do. I hate admitting that, but yeah, a lot of the time I kind of arrange it so nobody sees the full amount.

Like with my wife, I’ll sit down for dinner and act like I’m not all that hungry, or I’ll just eat a normal-looking plate and say I’m fine. And then later, once she’s doing something else or she’s settled in, I’ll go out to the truck or out toward the garage where the extra food is, and that’s when I eat more. It’s not just that I happen to be alone — it’s more like I’m waiting until I can be alone, because I’d be really embarrassed for her to see how much I’m actually putting away.

I think part of me is trying to keep up this picture like, “No, I’m normal, I’m not overeating,” but then I’m sneaking around afterward. It makes me feel pretty ashamed, honestly.
